summary: This defensive disclosure compiles the therapeutic use, molecular mechanism, dosing protocol, and clinical and preclinical evidence for magnesium L-threonate in age-related cognitive decline under a CC0 public-domain dedication. The submission provides comprehensive enabling detail, thoroughly surveys granted patents and peer-reviewed literature, and accurately describes the clinical and cellular evidence without overstating efficacy. As a prior-art defensive publication, it meets all criteria for inclusion in Priorroot.
strengths: High level of enabling detail including chemical identifiers (CAS 778571-57-6, IUPAC, molecular formula, elemental magnesium fraction), exact oral dosing (2,000 mg/day providing ~144 mg elemental Mg), divided schedule, and monitoring parameters.

Meticulous and factually accurate citation of foundational preclinical and clinical literature (Slutsky et al. 2010, Sun et al. 2016, Liu et al. 2016, and Lopresti & Smith 2026), verified against published records.
Comprehensive 10-step mechanistic breakdown distinguishing threonate's unique GLUT-mediated neuronal entry from other magnesium counter-anions.
Objective appraisal of clinical trial limitations, including sample size constraints, healthy younger cohorts, domain-specific effects, and commercial affiliations of original patent holders.
Clear and unambiguous CC0 1.0 Universal public-domain dedication serving defensive prior-art purposes.
weaknesses: The primary clinical indication is age-related cognitive decline, yet one of the two primary human RCTs cited (Lopresti & Smith, 2026) enrolled young adults (ages 18–45) with subjective sleep dissatisfaction rather than an elderly cognitive decline cohort.
Synthesizes established literature without presenting new experimental formulations, combinations, or delivery systems beyond what is already published in scientific journals.
suggestions: Clarify in the primary indication section how the young-adult data from the 2026 trial directly translates to elderly age-related cognitive decline versus preserving normative cognitive performance.
Expand on pharmacokinetics and bioavailability comparisons with newer liposomal or combined nootropic delivery platforms to broaden the anticipatory scope of the disclosure.

claims.text: In a 2026 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (n=100, 6 weeks, 2 g/day Magtein®), the MgT group showed significantly greater improvement on the NIH Cognitive Toolbox Total Cognition Composite score compared to placebo (p=0.043).
claims.source: Lopresti AL, Smith SJ. Frontiers in Nutrition (2026), 12:1729164, PMID: 41601871

claims.text: MgT treatment was associated with a 7.5-year reduction in estimated brain cognitive age based on NIH Toolbox normative data.
claims.source: Lopresti AL, Smith SJ. Frontiers in Nutrition (2026), 12:1729164, PMID: 41601871

claims.text: Increasing brain magnesium using a newly developed magnesium compound (magnesium-L-threonate, MgT) leads to the enhancement of learning abilities, working memory, and short- and long-term memory in rats, with higher density of synaptophysin-/synaptobrevin-positive puncta in DG and CA1 subregions of hippocampus.
claims.source: Slutsky I, Abumaria N, et al. Neuron (2010), 65(2):165-177, PMID: 20152124

claims.text: Two key U.S. patents (US 8,178,118 and US 8,142,803) held by Magceutics/AIDP claim magnesium L-threonate compositions for cognitive function and neurological disorders.
claims.source: USPTO Grants US 8,178,118 B2 and US 8,142,803 B2, Assignee: Magceutics, Inc.
